_comment: THE DRAW PROMOTION MUST STAND DOWN WHEN THE DRAW SPEND DOES --
MTG_COMBO_OFF_DRAW_UNPROMOTE.
This is fixture 10's board -- the user's seed-9 turn-4 frame -- with two deliberate changes: the
Living Wish is ON TOP of the library, and the opponent's library is SIX cards.  Fixture 10 itself
must stay ABSENT (its 50-card deck-out is genuinely out of reach at this board's net) and still
does; this variant isolates the loop's own economics with the dig and the kill both small enough
to finish.
Conservatory (+Wild Growth) = 2, Kitchen (+Overgrowth) = 3, Conservatory = 1, Mariposa = 1, and
Cloud of Faeries untaps TWO against Emiel's {3}.  All FOUR of those lands are draw/investigate
sources, so ApplyBlinkLoop's untap-priority set promotes all four -- and the set is consulted in
battlefield order, so the two slots go to a bare Conservatory and Mariposa (the {C} reservation)
rather than to the Overgrowth'd Kitchen.  Refund 3 against a cost of 3: **net ZERO**.
That promotion is correct only while the loop can CASH it.  The spend is `want_draw`, which goes
FALSE the instant a draw turns up the Living Wish -- and the promotion was computed once before
iteration 0 and never revisited.  So from the moment the dig SUCCEEDS the loop is pinned to lands
it will never activate again, banks nothing, and the Living Wish sits in hand against a {1}{G} +
{1}{U} it can never afford in one payment:
[finish] calls=60 hand=0 wish=0 no-mana=58 none-found=60
Withdrawing the promotion when the spend stands down restores the yield order for the rest of the
loop -- which is exactly what the ordered-set doctrine at the set's construction prescribes:
'Promoting a sink the loop cannot cash is a measured LOSS ... The two go on and off together,
ALWAYS.'  Session 14b fixed the ENTRY condition; this fixes the MID-LOOP one.
A/B on this fixture (one binary):
default                           -> x24, COMBO OFF verified, opponent decked
MTG_COMBO_OFF_DRAW_UNPROMOTE=0    -> x24, offered but NOT verified, the apply does not win
On the same board at the shipped 50-card opponent library the counters go from
`wish=0 no-mana=58` to `wish=1 hand=1 no-mana=0` -- the finish CHAIN completes either way now;
what the 50-card version still cannot do is pay fifty {C} pips at one per untap, which is why
fixture 10 stays absent.
